findings.claim: ReportIfLocatedInCompilation drops only diagnostics with an in-source location outside the compilation. Diagnostics with no location (Location.None, which the guarded null-location paths now produce) still pass through. For a closed generic struct from a referenced assembly, MsgPack004 (MemberNeedsKey) is now reported with a null location. Users who previously saw no diagnostic, because the type was skipped, may now get a location-less MsgPack004 error. L2 lists MsgPack004 as an Error, so this could fail builds. L8 says metadata types deliberately get no diagnostics.

receipt_plan.detail: Analyzer test: lib defines [MessagePackObject] struct Item<T> with a public property lacking [Key], and app uses Item<int> as a member of a [MessagePackObject]. Assert that the app build reports no MsgPack004/MsgPack003/MsgPack005 diagnostics on Item. If the Location.None diagnostic slips through, it fails.

findings.claim: The wrapper changes reportDiagnostic for every analyzer diagnostic, not only the metadata crash path. Diagnostics whose location is in a syntax tree not contained in this.compilation are now silently dropped. This can happen with a partial or generated tree, or when the TypeCollector is given a compilation other than the one being analyzed. Users could lose existing MsgPack0xx warnings or errors without opting in.

receipt_plan.detail: Run the existing analyzer test suite (MsgPack003 through MsgPack018 verifiers) on base and head and compare the reported diagnostics. Add a case with a diagnostic located in a generated or other-tree file and check it is still reported.
